problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for $\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}},$ given by

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}=x+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{7}{x}^{7}+⋯,\,x\in (-1,1)
$$

using sigma notation.
worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =x \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{1}{7}{x}^{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{{x}^{2\cdot 0+1}}{2\cdot 0+1} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{{x}^{2\cdot 1+1}}{2\cdot 1+1} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2\cdot 2+1}}{2\cdot 2+1} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{{x}^{2\cdot 3+1}}{2\cdot 3+1}\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{2n+1}\,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{\frac{1+x}{1-x}}={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{2n+1}.
$$
